reason: The Hebrew leaders depicted in this passage (Moses and God/the angel of God) demonstrate protective and supportive behavior toward the Hebrew people, not antagonism. When the people express fear and complain to Moses about being led to die in the wilderness, Moses responds with reassurance: 'Do not fear, stand firm and see the salvation of the Lord which he will work for you today.' Additionally, God actively intervenes on behalf of the people by moving the angel and pillar of cloud between the Egyptian and Israelite camps to protect them, then performing the miracle of the Red Sea to deliver the Israelites from Egyptian pursuit. These actions demonstrate leadership that is beneficent and protective, the opposite of antagonistic.
